newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon refuses to hand over smuggler to Bonn.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon refuses to hand over smuggler to Bonn.

text.p: Lebanon has rejected a German request to extradite a businessman of dual Lebanese-German nationality wanted for smuggling chemical weapons equipment from Germany to Libya, judicial sources said on Wednesday.

They said prosecutor-general Adnan Addoum found the demand to extradite Berge Balanian "inconsistent with Lebanese laws" as he was still a Lebanese citizen despite obtaining the German nationality in 1973.

"Under Lebanese laws a Lebanese citizen who commits a crime outside his country is prosecuted by judicial authorities in Lebanon," sources cited Addoum as saying in his reply to the German authorities.

Balanian, who was wanted on an international arrest warrent, has been in detention since Lebanese police arrested him on October 14 at a Beirut airport cafe on charges of "disturbing Lebanon's relations with foreign countries".
The German federal crime office in Wiesbaden has said Balanian was wanted for exporting state-of-the-art equipment to Libya for mixing poison gases.
Balanian denied the charges saying he only exported empty boxes for electrical equipment to Libya between 1992-1994, Lebanese judicial sources said.
German police say equipment to mix poison gases was illegally sent to Libya from Germany in 1990-93, contrary to German arms control laws.
German prosecutors believe the equipment was bought by the businessman's firms then sent to the Libyan port of Tripoli via Belgian companies that Belanian owns.
U.S. officials accused Libya earlier this year of trying to build an underground chemical weapons plant.
